title: chore(reposts): polish residual repost interaction paths (#4203)
body:
Refs #4203 — third execution item ("residual polish") under the weekly reposts coordination parent. Owner-facing visibility (#4173) shipped via PR #4172; cold-start hardening (#3522, #3533, #3534) is in place and #3523 is deferred. This PR closes the residual-polish bucket.

## Summary

Two thematically related fixes on the repost interaction paths:

- **Observability symmetry.** `VideoInteractionsBloc._publishLike` wraps its generic catch with `Reportable(e, context: '_publishLike')` so the `DivineBlocObserver` forwards the failure to Crashlytics. `_publishRepost` used a bare `addError(e, st)` — repost publish failures were silently dropped at the dashboard. This PR wraps it with `Reportable` to mirror the like path, and lifts the two `context:` identifiers into a `VideoInteractionsReportableSites` constants class per `.claude/rules/error_handling.md` (2+ sites graduate to a per-feature constants class).

- **Reposters-fetch unification.** The metadata sheet's "Reposted by" chips used the legacy `VideoEventService.getRepostersForVideo`, which only queries Kind 16 with the `e` tag, doesn't filter Kind 5 deletions, and doesn't merge across the `a` tag. The engagement-list screen shipped in PR #4172 uses the canonical `RepostsRepository.fetchEventReposters`, which queries Kind 6 + 16, filters deletions per author, and merges `e` + `a` tags for addressable events. This PR points the cubit at the canonical method so both surfaces show the same reposter set, and removes the legacy service method (the cubit was its only production caller).

## Files changed

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `lib/blocs/video_interactions/reportable_sites.dart` | New `VideoInteractionsReportableSites` constants class. |
| `lib/blocs/video_interactions/video_interactions_bloc.dart` | Wrap `_publishRepost` catch with `Reportable`; both sites use the constants. |
| `lib/widgets/video_feed_item/metadata/video_reposters_cubit.dart` | DI swap (`VideoEventService` → `RepostsRepository`); accepts optional `addressableId`. |
| `lib/widgets/video_feed_item/metadata/metadata_expanded_sheet.dart` | Reads `repostsRepositoryProvider` and threads `video.addressableId` to the cubit. |
| `lib/services/video_event_service.dart` | Delete `getRepostersForVideo` (only production caller migrated). |
| `test/blocs/video_interactions/video_interactions_bloc_test.dart` | Mirror the like-side `Reportable<Object>` assertion on the repost failure path. |
| `test/widgets/video_feed_item/metadata/video_reposters_cubit_test.dart` | Retarget mocks to `RepostsRepository`; preserve the `#3734` emit-after-close regression tests; add an addressable-id pass-through assertion. |
| `test/widgets/video_feed_item/actions/more_action_button_test.dart`, `test/widgets/video_feed_item/video_overlay_actions_description_test.dart`, `test/screens/feed/feed_video_overlay_test.dart` | Swap the `getRepostersForVideo` mocks for `fetchEventReposters` mocks on `repostsRepositoryProvider`. |
| `test/services/video_event_service_reposters_test.dart` | Deleted along with the underlying method. |

## Out of scope

- Migrating `metadata_expanded_sheet.dart` from `ProviderScope.containerOf` to `ConsumerWidget` + `ValueKey` per the state_management.md Riverpod → BlocProvider bridging rule. The sheet is a transient modal that dies on dismiss, so the stale-capture failure mode the rule defends against doesn't apply here. Filed as a separate consideration if a future change makes the sheet long-lived.
- `ProfileRepostedVideosBloc` `addError` consistency (Round 1 Candidate C). Its failure paths are sync/network errors that the error_handling.md matrix says should stay out of Crashlytics; the bloc's current bare-log behavior is matrix-correct.
- Cross-device count drift and double-tap UX known limitations from PR #3430.

title: chore: Gate Nostr side effects on session readiness
body:
## Description

Users could lose push registration on cold launch because auth could be ready before Nostr could sign yet.
This change separates identity readiness from Nostr readiness and makes signer-dependent work wait for the matching ready client.
That matters because push registration, notification preferences, and blocklist sync all publish Nostr events.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3929

## Type of Change

- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] 🧹 Code refactor
- [ ] ✅ Build configuration change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🗑️ Chore

## Summary

Auth state now means the app knows who the user is.
It no longer means the Nostr client is ready to sign and publish.
The app now waits for an explicit ready session before running side effects that need the signer.

## What Changed

The flow now carries the ready pubkey and client together.
Work that publishes through Nostr rejects stale sessions and queues preferences until the matching session is ready.
Sign-out also runs outgoing push deregistration before signer teardown.

- Added `NostrSessionReadiness` and kept `isNostrReadyProvider` as a compatibility shim.
- Moved push registration, token refresh, preference publishing, push deregistration, and blocklist sync to ready-session or pre-teardown paths.
- Added warning-only wrappers so non-critical push publish failures do not escape async listeners.
- Added regression tests for cold launch, account switch, teardown ordering, queued preferences, and async error handling.

## Testing

I rebased onto latest `origin/main` and ran the full Flutter checks.
The analyzer found no issues, and the full test suite passed with 8,383 passing tests and 400 skipped tests.

- `git fetch https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile.git main:refs/remotes/origin/main && git rebase origin/main`
- `flutter analyze`
- `flutter test`

## Risks

The main risk is lifecycle ordering around sign-out and account switch.
The new tests cover the flows that could use a stale or placeholder Nostr client.
Identity-only listeners such as routing and Zendesk still use auth state.

title: feat(auth): add under-16 family guidance flow
body:
Closes #3532

## Summary
This PR adds the client-side under-16 family guidance flow and the restricted-account review surfaces that route affected users into it.

## What Changed
- adds a welcome-screen entry point for under-16 family guidance
- adds the `/account-review` route family for welcome and moderation entry points
- adds a fail-closed checking route while authenticated moderation status is loading
- hard-gates restricted accounts to the allowed review, support, and moderation-message paths
- adds the public under-13 guidance screen and the restricted under-13 parent-support screen
- adds the 13-15 parent-consent screen and parent-contact submission screen
- sets the canonical support email to `support@divine.video`
- hosts family, kids, and age-review resources at paths on `divine.video` (e.g. `divine.video/family`) instead of separate subdomains
- fixes the support-email share fallback so the prepared body/instructions are preserved
- adds localized generic error states, Divine icon/accessibility cleanup, and focused widget/service tests

## Product Boundaries In This PR
- Under 13: parent or guardian must contact Divine support by email.
- Age 13 to 15: the parent or guardian email path is the supported handoff in this PR.
- This PR does not add private media upload, moderator tooling in other repos, or new backend review workflows.

title: fix(ios-camera): restart audio capture session around AVAudioSession reconfigure
body:
## Description


Fixes muted audio in recordings on iOS when the user interacts with another audio app (Spotify, a phone call, Siri, an alarm) before or during a recording.

## Why

iOS sends an `AVAudioSession.interruptionNotification` when another app takes the shared audio session. Before this change the plugin had no observer for that notification, so:

1. The session stayed in an interrupted (deactivated) state — no mic input — but `captureOutput(_:didOutput:from:)` kept running and appended silent AAC buffers to the asset writer, producing a video with a flat-line audio track.
2. After the interruption ended, the audio capture session was never restarted, so subsequent recordings were also muted until the app was relaunched.

## Manual test plan

1. Start a recording.
2. Trigger an interruption (receive a phone call, start Spotify, or
   ask Siri a question) and then dismiss it.
3. Stop the recording — verify audio is present for the portion before
   the interruption.
4. Start a new recording immediately after the interruption — verify
   audio is present throughout.
5. Repeat with Bluetooth headset connected.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3881 Closes #4171

title: feat(inbox): redesign conversation screen and inbox previews
body:
Closes #4287 ## Description End-to-end redesign of the DM screens (Messages tab and a single conversation). Touches the top "Contacts" carousel, the conversation list rows, the conversation header, the messages surface card, the message bubbles, the shared-video-in-DM card, the long-press action menus, and the report flow. Also fixes an inbox correctness bug (last-message preview was reading a denormalized column that could go stale), expands the app-bar icon button tap target to a true 48×48, unifies the DM-message and video report flows on one bottom sheet, and migrates eight DM-screen hardcoded English strings to \`context.l10n\`. ### A note on scope The supporting changes outside \`lib/screens/inbox\` might look unrelated to the DM-screen scope at first glance. While polishing the conversation header and the in-bubble shared-video card, I needed two cross-surface guarantees to also hold — those fixes only made sense applied consistently across every surface they touch, otherwise the same data would render differently on the conversation screen versus everywhere else. - \`lib/widgets/profile/profile_header_widget.dart\` — only a rename: \`_truncateNpubForDisplay\` (the helper that produces \`npub1xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx…\` for the profile screen subtitle) is now public so the conversation header can fall back to the same identifier shape when the participant has no NIP-05. Two surfaces, one helper. Letting the conversation header invent its own truncation would have meant the same user showed two different secondary identifiers depending on which screen you opened. - \`lib/widgets/report_content_dialog.dart\` — generalized to take either a video or an \`(eventId, authorPubkey)\` pair. The bottom sheet that opens from the home-feed video overlay's Report action and the bottom sheet that opens from a DM bubble's long-press > Report are now the same widget with the same UX (reason cards, "Other"-expands-to-details, in-sheet confirmation). The legacy \`ReportMessageDialog\` AlertDialog is gone. - \`packages/divine_ui/lib/src/app_bar/divine_app_bar_icon_button.dart\` — fixes a 40×40 tap target that should always have been 48×48 (the 4 px halo around the visible pill was previously decorative, not tappable). Caught while reviewing the conversation header; the fix applies everywhere \`DiVineAppBarIconButton\` is used. - \`packages/dm_repository/lib/src/dm_repository.dart\` — the inbox preview was reading the conversations table's denormalized \`lastMessageContent\` / \`lastMessageTimestamp\`, which can go stale when an older gift wrap arrives after a newer one during backfill. Reworked the read pipeline to overlay the actual latest message from \`direct_messages\` on every emit; messages-table is the source of truth. In an ideal world these would be separate PRs. ## Summary
The For You feed appears to be resurfacing repeated and stale videos instead of prioritizing videos the viewer has not yet watched.

Reported behavior from Rabble:
- Feed is repeating videos
- Feed is showing videos from ~2 months ago and older
- Goal is to ensure For You shows users new videos they have not yet watched

Companion backend investigation: divine-funnelcake issue #251

We need to verify whether the client-side For You experience is correctly requesting, tracking, and filtering feed items, and whether any mobile-side state / pagination behavior is contributing to repeated or stale results.

- Is divine-mobile correctly requesting the intended For You feed / cursor / refresh behavior?
- Is the client tracking watch / impression state in a way that could support de-duping or suppressing already-viewed videos?
- Are pagination, refresh, cache, or session-restoration behaviors causing already-seen items to reappear too aggressively?
- Is the app correctly handling backend responses, or is client logic reordering / reusing stale items?
- What mobile-side telemetry or safeguards are missing to detect and reduce repeated For You results?

- Audit For You feed fetch / pagination / refresh logic in mobile

Document root cause(s) and define the client-side changes needed so users are reliably shown fresh, not-yet-watched videos with fewer obvious repeats / stale resurfacing.

title: fix(search): drop idle placeholder on Explore → Search with prefilled query
body:
## Summary

Tapping into Explore's search bar and typing 2+ characters auto-pushes `/search-results/:query` after a 300ms debounce. The destination then flashed **"Enter a search query / Discover something interesting"** for another ~300–600ms before BLoCs were dispatched and section skeletons appeared. On slow networks the window stretched, reading as a flash, error, or hang. This PR makes the destination drop the idle placeholder when a route arg query is pending, and dispatch `*QueryChanged` events synchronously on AppBar mount so the BLoCs advance from `initial` this same frame.

Closes #3802. Companion to parent epic #3801.

## Root cause

`SearchResultsView` keyed the idle short-circuit on `VideoSearchBloc.state.status == initial` alone. That signal correctly identifies "no query entered" (the load-bearing PR #3199 fix for #3023's infinite skeleton) but does NOT distinguish it from "query just arrived as a route arg, AppBar dispatch is still pending its 300ms UI debounce."

## Changes

- `lib/screens/search_results/view/search_results_view.dart` — add optional `String initialQuery = ''`. Gate the idle short-circuit on `initialQuery.trim().length < minSearchQueryLength` so it matches the BLoC handlers' own gate exactly. Falls through to sections (whose own skeletons render on `initial || loading/searching` with empty results) when a searchable query is pending. Inline comment cites PR #3199 / #3023 so a future reader doesn't simplify the conditional back to the buggy form.
- `lib/screens/search_results/view/search_results_page.dart` — pass `initialQuery` from `_SearchResultsBody` to `SearchResultsView` (1 line).
- `lib/screens/search_results/widgets/search_results_app_bar.dart` — reorder `initState` so the controller text is seeded BEFORE the listener is attached. When `initialQuery.isNotEmpty`, dispatch `*QueryChanged` events synchronously to all four BLoCs. The BLoCs' `debounceRestartable` still applies; same-query dedup guards coalesce any late-arriving event. Focus model intentionally untouched — that's sibling issue #3020 / #3803 territory.

All 5 entry points to `SearchResultsPage` go through `SearchResultsPage(initialQuery: query)` (Explore auto-push, `@mention` link tap, universal link, deep link, GoRoute), so this fix applies uniformly.

### Commit history

1. `1f99c2b6` — initial fix.
2. `2407333d` — self-review follow-up: tighten the view's idle gate from `isEmpty` to `trim().length < minSearchQueryLength` so reachable edge cases (whitespace-only or 1-char deep links like `/search-results/a` and `/search-results/%20%20`) don't render infinite skeletons (a #3023-class regression in the corner). Two extra regression tests pin the corrected behavior.

## Scope clarification

Per the issue body: "Do not collapse this issue into keyboard/focus behavior. They are related, but not identical." This PR is scoped to the intermediate-state symptom only. The focus and keyboard work belongs to:

- #3020 — keyboard collapses (assigned to @untreu2)
- #3803 — canonical focus behavior (assigned to @NotThatKindOfDrLiz)

The parent epic #3801 calls for these three children to land as one cohesive transition PR (Gate 2). I scoped this PR to #3802 alone; bundling is the epic driver's call.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter test test/screens/search_results/` → **85 passing**
- [x] `flutter test test/blocs/{video,user,hashtag,list}_search test/blocs/search_results_filter` → **119 passing**
- [x] `flutter test test/screens/explore_screen_pure_test.dart` → 12 passing
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` → no issues
- [x] `dart format` → clean

New test coverage:
- `search_results_view_test.dart` — new `with non-empty initialQuery` group asserts `SearchSectionInitialState` does NOT render when `initialQuery` is non-empty + status is initial, and that the all-filter section list renders instead. Plus two regression tests pinning the whitespace-only and sub-min-length cases to the idle placeholder (cures the #3023-class edge case).
- `search_results_app_bar_test.dart` — adds missing `_MockListSearchBloc` mock (the existing setUp had a gap), plus three new tests: synchronous dispatch on non-empty `initialQuery`, NO dispatch on empty `initialQuery`, and no double-dispatch after the 300ms debounce window elapses.
- Existing idle-state tests preserved verbatim — PR #3199's load-bearing behavior is unchanged for the empty-query path.

## Manual device testing guide

### What changed (one-paragraph context for QA)

When you typed 2+ characters in Explore's search bar and the app auto-pushed to `/search-results/:query`, you saw a brief "Enter a search query / Discover something interesting" placeholder for ~300–600ms before search results loaded — especially noticeable on slow networks. After this fix, the destination shows section skeletons immediately and lands on real results once they arrive. The empty-query case (opening the search screen directly) still shows the "Enter a search query" placeholder as before.

### Build

Pick one:

- **Preview web build** (fastest, no local setup): open the `Mobile PR Preview` link from this PR's checks. The bot posts a `https://<hash>.openvine-app.pages.dev` URL on every push.
- **Local install** on the device:
  ```bash
  git fetch origin
  git checkout fix/3802-search-intermediate-state
  cd mobile
  flutter pub get
  flutter run --release   # release matters — debug mode is slower and masks the symptom
  ```
- **TestFlight / internal build** if one is cut later — pull the build tagged with this PR's SHA.

Notes:
- The bug is more visible in `release` than `debug` (debug is slow anyway, so any flash is harder to attribute).
- The bug is most visible on slow networks. Throttle to "Slow 3G" via iOS Settings → Developer → Network Link Conditioner (or Android Developer Options → Networking → Network type → "GPRS"), or use a proxy throttle.

### Golden path — primary repro from issue #3802

1. Launch the app. Sign in if needed.
2. Tap the **Explore** bottom-nav tab.
3. Tap the search bar at the top of Explore.
4. Type `hello` (or any 2+ character query). **Stop typing** and wait.
5. After ~300ms the app navigates to the search results screen.

What to look for (frame-by-frame):

| Frame | Before this fix (broken) | After this fix (correct) |
|---|---|---|
| Navigation completes | Screen renders with a centered search icon + **"Enter a search query"** + **"Discover something interesting"** | Screen renders with shimmer **skeletons** for People / Lists / Tags / Videos sections |
| ~300–600ms later | Skeletons appear (the placeholder fades) | (same skeletons continue, no flash transition) |
| Results arrive | Real results render | Real results render |

- **Pass criteria**: at no point during the transition does the "Enter a search query" copy appear.
- **Fail signal**: if you see "Enter a search query" or "Discover something interesting" even briefly, the fix didn't apply.

Tip: if you can't catch it visually, screen-record at 60 fps and step through frames.

### Slow-network case — the issue's "feels like a hang" complaint

Same steps as Golden path, but throttle to Slow 3G first.

- **Pass**: skeletons hold for as long as the network needs, then results land. No misleading "Enter a query" text. No fallback to an error state until/unless results genuinely fail.
- **Fail**: the "Enter a search query" copy appears, OR the screen looks empty/blank for any period.

### Direct entry to /search-results (regression check for #3023 — DO NOT skip)

This is the load-bearing case from PR #3199. **This must still work the OLD way.**

Two ways to trigger:

A. Universal/deep link with empty query — open the app from a `divine.video/search-results/` link (no query) if you can construct one, OR

B. In the running app: Explore → tap search bar → land on `/search-results/` with no query in the field.

- **Pass**: centered "Enter a search query" / "Discover something interesting" placeholder renders. **This is correct** — it was the #3023 fix.
- **Fail**: shimmer skeletons render indefinitely (that's #3023 reopening).

### Edge cases — sub-min-length & whitespace-only query (the F1 finding addressed in commit 2)

Reachable via deep / universal links — try if you can construct them, otherwise skip:

1. Open `divine.video/search-results/a` (single character) — or build a URL pointing at `/search-results/a` and open it from another app.
2. Open `divine.video/search-results/%20%20%20` (whitespace-only, URL-encoded).

- **Pass for both**: idle placeholder "Enter a search query" renders. (BLoCs gate on `length >= 2` so sub-min queries never reach the network; the view correctly treats them as idle.)
- **Fail**: shimmer skeletons render indefinitely.

### Other entry paths — same expected behavior

These all converge through `SearchResultsPage(initialQuery: ...)` so they should all behave consistently:

1. Tap an `@username` mention in a comment (links via `linkified_text`) — should land on search with the username pre-filled, **no misleading placeholder**.
2. Open the app from a universal link `https://divine.video/search-results/<query>` — same.
3. Open from a push-notification deep link with a search term — same.

- **Pass**: skeletons + results. No "Enter a search query" flash.

### Focus / keyboard — explicitly NOT in scope here

This fix does NOT change focus or keyboard behavior. Those are tracked separately in:
- **#3020** (keyboard collapses when typing in Explore → search page) — assigned to @untreu2
- **#3803** (canonical focus model) — assigned to @NotThatKindOfDrLiz

For #3802 QA: **don't flag** keyboard or focus issues against this PR. The destination field will not auto-focus when navigated with a pre-filled query — that's the existing behavior and intentionally untouched.

### Filters & deep search — confirm nothing else regressed

1. Land on `/search-results/hello` (golden path).
2. Tap the **filter pill** (top-right). Switch between All / People / Videos / Tags / Lists.

- **Pass**: each filter renders its skeletons → results. No "Enter a search query" appears on any filter tab even before results arrive.
- **Fail**: any filter renders the empty-query placeholder.

### Empty results — make sure we don't show idle instead of empty

1. Search a query with truly no results (e.g. random keyboard mash like `xqzqzqzq`).
2. Wait for results to settle (~1–5 seconds).

- **Pass**: each section shows its appropriate empty-state ("No results found for X" / "Try a different search term"). **Not** "Enter a search query."
- **Fail**: the idle placeholder shows after BLoCs have completed.

### Error/timeout (people search) — confirm degraded-empty UI

Same as above on a flaky network. If NIP-50 user search times out:

- **Pass**: People section shows the retry affordance (per the #3791 / #3804 fix that already landed). Other sections show their results or empty states.
- **Fail**: idle placeholder shows instead of the retry UI.

### Sign-off checklist

```
[ ] Golden path: type `hello` in Explore, no "Enter a search query" flash
[ ] Slow-3G repro: same, with throttle on
[ ] Direct-entry (empty query): "Enter a search query" placeholder DOES render
[ ] Sub-min-length deep link `/search-results/a`: idle placeholder renders
[ ] Whitespace-only deep link `/search-results/%20%20`: idle placeholder renders
[ ] @mention tap → search: skeletons not placeholder
[ ] Universal link with query: skeletons not placeholder
[ ] Filter switch: each filter shows skeletons until results, never placeholder
[ ] Empty result (mash query): empty-state not placeholder
[ ] People-timeout: retry UI not placeholder
[ ] Devices: iOS + Android, recent + min-supported OS
```

If any row fails, file a comment on this PR with the device, OS, network condition, and a screen recording.

## Notes for reviewers

- The doc comment over the `isIdle` conditional in `search_results_view.dart` is intentional — `tests-guard-intentional-workarounds` precedent. Don't simplify it back to `isInitialStatus` alone or #3023 reopens.
- The idle gate uses `initialQuery.trim().length < minSearchQueryLength` rather than `isEmpty` so it mirrors the BLoC handlers' own gate exactly. The looser `isEmpty` form regressed reachable edge cases in commit 1; commit 2 tightened it.
- Parent epic #3801 Gate 1 (auto-push vs explicit submit) is owned by Product / Design and unresolved. This fix is safe under either outcome: if Gate 1 keeps auto-push, the misleading state is fixed; if Gate 1 removes auto-push from Explore, the universal-link / deep-link / `@mention`-link entry paths still benefit from this fix.

Closes #3596. Advances epic #4208.

## Summary

Final step of the dual-notification-system retirement. The legacy
Riverpod `relay_notifications_provider.dart` + `notification_model_converter.dart`
stack had exactly one remaining production consumer on `main` after
the four sibling PRs that landed today
(#4247 / #4271 / #4276 / #4277). This PR migrates that consumer
(`notification_settings_screen.dart`'s `_markAllAsRead`) to
`NotificationRepository.markAllAsRead()` and deletes the entire
legacy stack plus its five test files.

The BLoC-based `lib/notifications/` feature is now the only
notifications stack in the app.

## What changed

| Commit | Change |
|--------|--------|
| `docs(notifications)` | Brainstorm doc with the scope reasoning |
| `feat(l10n)` | New `notificationSettingsMarkAllAsReadFailed` ARB key + regen |
| `refactor(notifications)` | Settings screen → `NotificationRepository`; stale doc comment in `notification_realtime_bridge.dart` refreshed |
| `test(notifications)` | New `notification_settings_screen_test.dart` (success / failure / disabled) |
| `refactor(notifications)` | Delete 8 legacy files (provider + .g.dart + converter + 5 tests) |

**Net change: −4,595 LOC** (5,067 deletions, 472 insertions). 4× the issue's "~1,000 LOC" estimate.

## Behaviour delta

`RelayNotifications.markAllAsRead()` silently swallowed server errors and always showed a green "All notifications marked as read" snackbar. `NotificationRepository.markAllAsRead()` rolls back its snapshot and rethrows on failure (PR #4034 → #4247 semantics). The settings screen now wraps the call in try/catch and surfaces failures as a red `VineTheme.error` snackbar with the new "Failed to mark all as read" copy. Strictly safer than the legacy "always confirm even when the write didn't reach the server" behaviour.

When `notificationRepositoryProvider` is null (early auth window), the action card's `onTap` is null — Material's built-in disabled affordance.

## Test plan

- [x] `dart format lib test integration_test` — clean
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — no issues
- [x] `dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` — no drift

- [ ] Manual Android: same two paths
- [ ] Manual account-switch: sign out → sign in fast → Settings → Notifications. Action card briefly disabled until repo wakes up; no crash

## Coverage

The 5 deleted test files (3,295 LOC) had their behaviour duplicated in `mobile/packages/notification_repository/test/` (refresh + mark-all-as-read + rollback + acceptRealtime, including the rollback semantics added by #4034) and in `test/notifications/` (BLoC feed, badge cubit, realtime bridge, view tests). No net coverage loss.

1. `notification_settings_screen.dart` carries four unpersisted local flags (`_systemEnabled`, `_pushNotificationsEnabled`, `_soundEnabled`, `_vibrationEnabled`) whose Switch widgets do nothing across app restarts.
2. Audit whether per-type toggles (likes / comments / follows / mentions / reposts) actually gate notification ingestion or are decorative.

title: perf(inbox): remove N+1 latest-message overlay queries in DmRepository
body:
## Summary
PR #4286 adds a read-time workaround in `mobile/packages/dm_repository/lib/src/dm_repository.dart` to repair stale inbox preview data by overlaying each conversation row with the actual latest message from `direct_messages`.

That workaround fixes correctness, but it introduces a new performance problem: every emission from `watchAcceptedConversations()` and `watchPotentialRequests()` now performs one `DirectMessagesDao.getMessagesForConversation(..., limit: 1)` query per conversation.

For users with many conversations, this turns a single conversations-stream update into an N+1 fan-out of DAO reads.

## Current implementation
PR #4286 changes these paths:
- `watchAcceptedConversations()` -> `.asyncMap(_overlayLatestMessages)`
- `watchPotentialRequests()` -> `.asyncMap(_overlayLatestMessages)`

`_overlayLatestMessages()` then does:
- iterate every `ConversationRow`
- call `getMessagesForConversation(row.id, limit: 1, ownerPubkey: _ownerPubkey)`
- copy the latest message fields back onto the domain model
- resort the list in memory by the overlaid timestamp

Relevant code in the PR:
- `mobile/packages/dm_repository/lib/src/dm_repository.dart:1667-1698`

## Why this matters
The workaround runs on every stream tick, not just on first load.

That means:
- 10 conversations -> 10 extra DAO reads per emit
- 100 conversations -> 100 extra DAO reads per emit
- every accepted-conversations refresh and every potential-requests refresh pays this cost

Even if the reads are parallelized with `Future.wait`, the app still performs one query per conversation, plus an in-memory resort, on every update. This is avoidable read amplification on a hot inbox path.

## Root cause
The comment added in PR #4286 documents the underlying correctness problem well: the denormalized `conversations.lastMessageContent` / `lastMessageTimestamp` fields can drift out of sync with the real latest message in `direct_messages`.

The overlay is compensating for write-path drift at read time.

## Desired outcome
Keep the correctness fix, but remove the per-conversation query fan-out.

## Candidate fixes
### Option A: batched latest-message query
Add a DAO method that fetches the latest message for many conversation ids in one query, for example:
- `getLatestMessagesForConversations(List<String> conversationIds, {required String ownerPubkey})`

Then replace the N queries in `_overlayLatestMessages()` with a single batched read and a map/join in memory.

### Option B: fix denormalized-column drift at the write path
Investigate why `conversations.lastMessageContent` and `lastMessageTimestamp` become stale during backfill / out-of-order gift-wrap arrival.

If the write path can guarantee the denormalized columns always reflect the actual latest message, the overlay can be removed entirely and the existing conversation-watch queries can remain the source of truth.

### Option C: hybrid transition
Ship a batched DAO read first to remove the N+1 cost, then follow with a write-path correctness fix and delete the overlay once the denormalized columns are trustworthy again.

## Acceptance criteria
- Inbox conversation streams no longer perform one `getMessagesForConversation(... limit: 1)` call per conversation on every emit.
- The inbox preview still shows the true latest message even when the conversation row is stale.
- Ordering remains based on the real latest message timestamp.
- Existing regression coverage for stale preview overlay remains intact or is updated to cover the new batched/corrected implementation.
- If the final fix relies on transitional code, include a linked `TODO(#issue)` with a clear removal plan.

## Regression tests to preserve
The tests added in PR #4286 should remain conceptually covered:
- overlays the latest message from `DirectMessageRow` over the denormalized row preview
- re-sorts conversations by the actual latest message timestamp
- file-message preview overlay behavior

## Context
Introduced while reviewing PR #4286.

This issue tracks removing the new N+1 inbox read-path debt without losing the correctness fix that motivated it.

title: fix(notifications): dedupe WS-first notifications against later REST loads
body:
## Description

Closes the symmetric gap left by PR #4247: a WebSocket arrival followed by a later REST pagination page containing the same Nostr event no longer duplicates the row (or duplicates a grouped contribution to an existing `(videoEventId, kind)` group).

### Root cause

`NotificationRepository._emitSnapshotForPage` deduped non-first pages by `existingIds = current.items.map((n) => n.id).toSet()`. WS-inserted items have `id = nostr_event_id` (bridge sets `model.id = event.id` → `RelayNotification.id = model.id` → `dedupeKey = id` since non-empty); REST-inserted items have `id = server_uuid` from `RelayNotification.fromJson(json)['id']`. The two ids never collide for the same logical event, so the same Nostr event flowed through both paths produced two snapshot rows.

PR #4247 closed the symmetric REST → WS direction by adding `_knownSourceEventIds` and the early return at `notification_repository.dart:260`. The reverse (WS → REST) had no equivalent gate inside `_emitSnapshotForPage`.

### Reproducing the bug (pre-PR)

1. Open inbox notifications on an account that can receive live notifications. The first REST page loads with cursor=`null` → `isFirstPage: true` → snapshot replaced (`notification_repository.dart:144`). `_lastCursor` is now non-null.
2. Stay on the inbox tab. From a second device, trigger a new notification (like, comment, follow) targeting the test account. The WS bridge (`notification_realtime_bridge.dart:64`) converts the realtime `NotificationModel` (with `id = event.id` = Nostr event id) into a `RelayNotification` (`id = sourceEventId = nostr_event_id`) and calls `acceptRealtime`. The row is prepended with `id = nostr_event_id`.
3. Scroll to the load-more threshold (`notifications_view.dart:75`) so `NotificationFeedLoadMore` fires. `getNotifications()` is called with the stored cursor → `isFirstPage: false` → APPEND path.
4. The REST page returns the same logical event with `id = server_uuid`, `sourceEventId = nostr_event_id`.
5. **Expected**: one row.
6. **Actual (pre-PR)**: two rows (or a duplicate contribution to an existing grouped video notification).

Refresh-from-scratch eventually clears the duplication because `refresh()` zeroes `_lastCursor` and the next emit is a full replace — so the bug is visible churn, not permanent corruption (the issue body says the same).

### Verifying the fix (post-PR)

Same steps 1–4. The pagination page no longer appends a duplicate:

- For standalone rows (`ActorNotification`): the new gate-2 `sourceEventIds` overlap detects that the REST item's `nostr_event_id` is already represented by the WS row and skips it.
- For grouped video notifications: gate-1 `(videoEventId, kind)` overlap merges the richer REST data into the existing WS row in place (preserving its position; rebuilding actors capped at `_maxGroupActors`; uniting `sourceEventIds`; `totalCount` = size of union).

### What changed

`mobile/packages/models/`:

- `NotificationItem` base gains `sourceEventIds: List<String>` (default `const []`). Subtypes pipe through ctor, `copyWith`, and `props`.

`mobile/packages/notification_repository/`:

- `_groupVideoAnchored`, `_mapActorAnchored`, and both `enrichOne` branches populate `sourceEventIds` from the underlying raws (skipping empties, mirroring the existing `_knownSourceEventIds` guard).
- `_mergeIntoExistingVideoGroup` unions `sourceEventIds` when a WS arrival merges into an existing group so the merged row carries every Nostr event it represents.
- New `_mergeAppendedVideoGroup` helper handles the symmetric "REST page → existing WS row" merge with locked semantics: set union for `sourceEventIds`; `totalCount` floored at `mergedActors.length` to keep the constructor invariant; existing-first actor order to match production pagination semantics; thumbnail / title / addressable id `_nonEmpty` fallback; **`commentText` picks from the side with the larger `timestamp`** (mirrors `_groupVideoAnchored`'s newest-wins and the surrounding `timestamp = max(...)` rule), falling back to the other side only when the newer side has no text.
- `_emitSnapshotForPage` for non-first pages now uses three gates: (1) `(videoEventId, type)` overlap → merge; (2) `sourceEventIds` overlap → skip; (3) `id` equality fallback → skip. First-page emit unchanged (REST first page is authoritative).

PR #4247's REST→WS guard (`_knownSourceEventIds` + `acceptRealtime` early return at line 260, plus the load-bearing test at `notification_repository_test.dart:1611`) is untouched.

### Follow-up

- **#4284** — techdebt: consolidate dedupe substrates (retire `_knownSourceEventIds` + `acceptRealtime` id-equality fallback into the new `sourceEventIds`-overlap source of truth). Tracked separately because the `refresh()`-then-WS semantic boundary needs its own regression test and the load-bearing test at `notification_repository_test.dart:1611` is the gate.

### Acceptance criteria mapping

- "WS-first → REST-later does not duplicate the same logical notification in the repository snapshot." — gates 1+2 in `_emitSnapshotForPage`.
- "Dedupe works for both standalone rows and grouped video notifications." — gates 1 (grouped) and 2 (standalone); covered by tests under `group('WS-first dedupe in page-merge (#4264)')`.
- "The chosen dedupe key is explicit and covered by tests." — typed `sourceEventIds: List<String>` on `NotificationItem`; new tests in both the model package and the repository package.
- "No regression to the existing REST-first → WS-later guard added in #4204." — `_knownSourceEventIds` and the `acceptRealtime` line-260 gate are untouched; PR #4247's test at `notification_repository_test.dart:1611` still passes verbatim.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4264

The notification snapshot now dedupes the common REST-first -> WS-later path by tracking `sourceEventId`, but the reverse case is still open: when a realtime WS notification arrives first in the current session, a later REST refresh or pagination can still append the same logical event again because the snapshot append path only dedupes by rendered item `id`.

## Assignee
`@realmeylisdev`

## Weekly Priority
`P2`

## Parent
- `#4200`

## Related
- `#4204`
- `#4208`

## Problem
Current behavior after `#4204`:
- WS-first: `NotificationRealtimeBridge` converts the realtime `NotificationModel` into a `RelayNotification` whose `id` is the Nostr event id.
- Later REST load: the same logical event comes back with the server UUID in `id` and the Nostr event id in `sourceEventId`.
- `_emitSnapshotForPage(...)` only dedupes appended items by `NotificationItem.id`, so the later REST page can still append a duplicate row or duplicate grouped contribution.

Refresh-from-scratch eventually replaces the snapshot and clears it, so this is not a permanent corruption bug, but it is still visible churn and leftover dual-path debt.

## Repro
1. Open inbox notifications on an account that can receive live notifications.
2. Trigger a new notification from a second device so it arrives over WS first.
3. Without leaving the session, trigger the REST path that pulls the same logical notification into the repository snapshot.
4. Observe that the same event can appear twice because WS and REST use different `id` values.

## Acceptance Criteria
- WS-first -> REST-later does not duplicate the same logical notification in the repository snapshot.
- Dedupe works for both standalone rows and grouped video notifications.
- The chosen dedupe key is explicit and covered by tests.
- No regression to the existing REST-first -> WS-later guard added in `#4204`.

## Notes
A likely fix is to extend page-merge dedupe to consider the same logical event identity used by realtime ingestion (`sourceEventId` / Nostr event id), not just the rendered item `id`. The final implementation should follow the current repository shape rather than layering a second cache.

title: Report dialog: require description when Other reason is selected

- Details text field is required when "Other" is selected
- Field label changes from "Additional details (optional)" to "Please describe the issue" to signal the requirement
- Validation error shown if user tries to submit without a description
- All other report reasons continue to work with optional details

## Context

Surfaced during relay admin category review — the "Other" bucket is only useful if reporters explain what they're flagging.

title: refactor(perf): replace polling timers with event-driven readiness signals (#3352)
body:
## Description

Three independent polling/timer coordination sites in `mobile/lib`
become event-driven. Closes the four acceptance criteria of #3352
without introducing new wall-clock timers or `Future.delayed`
workarounds.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3352

## Type of Change

- [x] 🧹 Code refactor

## What Changed

### Site A — `isNostrReady` (50 ms polling → one-shot `Completer`)

`isNostrReadyProvider` previously ran a `Timer.periodic(50ms, …)` until
`NostrClient.hasKeys` flipped true. Riverpod cannot observe that
transition through ref equality because `NostrClient.initialize()`
mutates the underlying `_nostr` instance in-place, so the workaround
was a busy poll on every cold start.

This PR exposes a one-shot `Future<void> get ready` on `NostrClient`
that resolves the first time `initialize()` completes.
`isNostrReadyProvider` now awaits that future once and invalidates
itself when it fires — zero idle wakeups on cold start. The
late-completion path is guarded against account-switch races by an
`identical(client, ...)` check before invalidating.

The sister polling site in `notificationServiceEnhanced` (a
`Future.delayed(500ms)` × 30 retry loop waiting for the same flip) is
replaced by the same `await client.ready` with a matching 15 s
timeout.

> Coordinated with PR #4162's broader `NostrSessionReadiness` redesign
> — that PR's compatibility shim for `isNostrReady` keeps the same
> provider name and value semantics, so this PR rebases cleanly on top
> of it.

### Site B — `RelayNotifications` (5-min `Timer` → FCM + lifecycle + pull)

After merged PR #4247 moved the badge + inbox feed onto
`NotificationRepository`'s reactive snapshot, the 5-min auto-refresh
`Timer` in `RelayNotifications` no longer drives any user-visible
state. The provider now refreshes on three explicit signals:

- **App resume** — `ref.listen<bool>(appForegroundProvider, …)` edge-
  triggers on the `false → true` transition. Re-emitting `true` (no
  edge) and `true → false` (pause) intentionally do nothing.
- **Foreground FCM message** — a subscription to
  `firebaseOnMessageProvider` calls `refresh()` whenever the divine
  push service delivers a foreground notification.
- **Explicit user action** — pull-to-refresh in
  `notifications_screen.dart` was already wired through `refresh()`.

Also removes the `_startAutoRefresh()` tail call inside `refresh()`
that quietly re-armed the timer, and the `ref.onResume` / `ref.onCancel`
timer hooks that surrounded it.

### Site C — `EmailVerificationCubit` (fixed 3 s → bounded backoff)

Replaces the fixed 3 s `Timer.periodic` with a recursive `Timer`
driven by a bounded backoff schedule (3, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21 s, capped at
30 s). The 15-min total budget stays the same, but the total poll
count drops from ~300 to ~33 — a 10× reduction in idle wakeups for
users who never click the verification link. First poll still fires
at +3 s, preserving snappy UX for fast clicks.

The dispose-cancellation contract is now pinned by two new tests:
- cubit-level "close leaves no pending timers" (`fakeAsync` proves the
  recursive scheduler unwinds cleanly).
- screen-level "calls stopPolling when widget is removed from tree
  without nav" (proves the screen's own `dispose()` cancels — not
  just the GoRouter teardown).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `isNostrReadyProvider` invalidates from an explicit readiness
  signal, not a 50 ms timer.
- [x] Relay notifications refresh on realtime events, app resume, or
  explicit user action instead of a persistent timer where feasible.
- [x] Email verification polling has bounded backoff and tests for
  cancellation on dispose / navigation.
- [x] No new arbitrary `Future.delayed` or tight-timer coordination is
  introduced.

## Testing

- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean.
- Scoped suites:
  - `test/blocs/email_verification` — 32 pass (4 new tests).
  - `test/screens/auth/email_verification_screen_test.dart` — 17 pass
    (1 new test).
  - `test/providers/relay_notifications_provider_test.dart`,
    `relay_notifications_insert_test.dart` — 46 pass.
  - `test/providers/relay_notifications_refresh_triggers_test.dart`
    — 5 pass (new file).
  - `test/providers/push_notification_sync_test.dart` — 6 pass.
  - `test/unit/providers/is_nostr_ready_provider_test.dart` — 7 pass
    (rewritten).
  - `test/providers/app_lifecycle_provider_test.dart` — 2 pass.
  - `test/notifications/**` — 250+ pass (regression sweep).
- Package: `mobile/packages/nostr_client` — 254 pass (5 new tests on
  the `ready` future, including error-path coverage).

## Test plan

- [ ] Manual on iOS: cold start with a previously-signed-in account
  and confirm no 50 ms-wakeup pattern appears in DevTools timeline.
- [ ] Manual on Android: background → foreground the app while on
  `/notifications-settings` and confirm the legacy notifications
  refresh once (not five-minute-later).
- [ ] Manual on iOS / Android: register a new account, leave the
  email unverified for >2 minutes, confirm OAuth poll count grows
  via the backoff schedule (not every 3 s).

## Coordination

- cc @dcadenas — Site A is logically subsumed by #4162's
  `NostrSessionReadiness` redesign. This PR's `NostrClient.ready`
  surface is additive and #4162 can land on top without conflict.
- cc @realmeylisdev (assignee) — #3352 is listed as related debt
  under #4208; this finishes the timer-cleanup half before the
  broader dual-system removal.

title: perf(async): replace readiness and notification polling timers with event-driven signals
body:
Source audit context: fresh `origin/main` worktree `.worktrees/audit-codebase-2026-04-24` at commit `33f6e026a`.
This issue was generated from the April 2026 codebase audit and includes file/line evidence from that snapshot.

## Severity
Medium

## Problem
Several readiness and notification flows use timers as coordination primitives, including tight 50ms Nostr readiness polling and periodic notification/email verification polling.

## Evidence
- mobile/lib/providers/app_providers.dart:1067-1085 polls nostrClient.hasKeys every 50ms.
- mobile/lib/providers/relay_notifications_provider.dart:96-102 keeps an auto-refresh Timer.
- mobile/lib/providers/relay_notifications_provider.dart:105-117 restarts the notification timer when backgrounded.
- mobile/lib/providers/relay_notifications_provider.dart:153-170 starts/stops timers from listener lifecycle.
- mobile/lib/blocs/email_verification/email_verification_cubit.dart:95-103 starts periodic polling.
- mobile/lib/screens/auth/email_verification_screen.dart:117-128 and :159-175 start polling in route modes.

## Impact
Polling creates unnecessary wakeups and brittle lifecycle coordination. Tight readiness polling is wasteful during startup and notification refresh can drift into auth/background edge cases.

## Recommended fix
Expose readiness as a stream/listenable from initialization instead of polling object fields. Prefer push/realtime invalidation and app-resume refresh over persistent timers where feasible.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] isNostrReadyProvider invalidates from an explicit readiness signal, not a 50ms timer.
- [ ] Relay notifications refresh on realtime events, app resume, or explicit user action instead of a persistent timer where feasible.
- [ ] Email verification polling has bounded backoff and tests for cancellation on dispose/navigation.
- [ ] No new arbitrary Future.delayed or tight timer coordination is introduced.

## Related issues
Likely overlap: #3151, #2444, #2447, #1948, #2701, #3167.

title: fix(notifications): throw typed exceptions from notification API methods
body:
## Description

`FunnelcakeApiClient.getNotifications` and `markNotificationsRead` silently caught all exceptions and non-200 responses, returning empty/failure DTOs instead of throwing the typed `FunnelcakeException` family that every other method in the file throws. Two layers of error-handling infrastructure were dead as a result:

- `NotificationRepository`'s mark-read rollback try/catch only fires on a throw, so the optimistic snapshot flip stayed in place even when the server returned 5xx — or when it returned `200` with `success: false`.
- `NotificationFeedBloc`'s `NotificationFeedStatus.failure` / `_FailureBody` retry widget / `notificationsFailedToLoad` l10n strings (translated to 16+ locales) only render when the repo throws, so users saw the empty state on a failed cold load — indistinguishable from a real empty inbox.

Both methods now follow the canonical `getVideosByAuthor` pattern: `isAvailable` guard, status-code throws of `FunnelcakeApiException`, `on TimeoutException` → `FunnelcakeTimeoutException`, `on FunnelcakeException { rethrow }`, generic `catch` → `FunnelcakeException`. `markNotificationsRead` additionally throws `FunnelcakeApiException(statusCode: 200, …)` when the server returns `200` with `success: false`, embedding the server-provided `error` string in the message so the repository rollback path fires consistently with the HTTP-error case. `NotificationRepository.getNotifications` swaps its swallow for a `rethrow` after preserving the structured `developer.log` line for triage. The BLoC and view layers need no changes — their failure paths were always correctly wired and just needed a real throw to react to.

**Existing tests** across `notification_repository_test.dart` and `notification_feed_bloc_test.dart` that stubbed the API to throw and asserted rollback / failure-status behavior **now exercise real production paths instead of dead code**.

Removes one bullet from #4208's "Relevant Debt" list.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3590

## Reproductions (pre-PR)

### Repro A — cold-load failure shows empty state instead of retry
1. Fresh launch in airplane mode; sign in.
2. Open Inbox → Notifications tab.
3. **Expected**: `_FailureBody` with "Failed to load notifications" + "Retry" button.
4. **Actual (pre-PR)**: empty state ("No notifications yet"), indistinguishable from a real empty inbox. The API silently returns `NotificationResponse(notifications: [], unreadCount: 0)`, the snapshot updates to empty, BLoC emits `loaded` status.

### Repro B — mark-read failure leaves optimistic flip in place
1. Open Inbox with one unread notification (badge=1).
2. Disable network.
3. Tap the notification.
4. **Expected**: row stays unread (rollback fires), badge stays at 1, error reaches `addError` for logging.
5. **Actual (pre-PR)**: row stays read (optimistic flip not rolled back), badge stays at 0. The API returns `MarkReadResponse(success: false, markedCount: 0)` instead of throwing, so the repository's rollback `catch` arm never executes.

### Repro C — refresh failure shows empty state
1. Load the inbox normally; some items appear.
2. Disable network; pull-to-refresh.
3. **Expected**: actionable retry UI.
4. **Actual (pre-PR)**: snapshot updates to empty (silent suppression), list shows "No notifications yet" replacing the previously visible items.

### Repro D — server-side soft-failure (200 / success:false) leaves optimistic flip in place
1. Open Inbox with one unread notification while the auth token has been server-rotated (so the relay rejects writes but returns a 200 with `{"success": false, "error": "token rejected"}`).
2. Tap the notification.
3. **Expected**: row stays unread, badge stays at 1, error reaches `addError`.
4. **Actual (pre-PR)**: row flips to read, badge zeroes, server actually rejected the write — the local read state diverges from server truth.

## Verification (post-PR)

- Repro A: `_FailureBody` renders with "Failed to load notifications" + "Retry" button. `NotificationFeedStatus.failure` finally fires.
- Repro B: row stays unread, badge stays at 1. The repository's rollback arm fires on the typed `FunnelcakeApiException` throw, restores the pre-write snapshot, then rethrows. The BLoC's `addError(e, s)` reaches `DivineBlocObserver` (not Crashlytics — per `error_handling.md` reportable matrix, network/IO/HTTP errors stay un-reported).
- Repro C: `_FailureBody` with retry replaces the misleading empty state. The user's data is preserved in the snapshot's `BehaviorSubject` value and reappears on a successful retry.
- Repro D: `markNotificationsRead` throws `FunnelcakeApiException(statusCode: 200, message: "Mark notifications read rejected by server: token rejected")`. The repository's rollback fires, snapshot returns to the pre-flip state, badge stays at 1.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `mobile/packages/funnelcake_api_client/lib/src/funnelcake_api_client.dart` | Rewrite `getNotifications` and `markNotificationsRead` to throw the typed `FunnelcakeException` family, mirroring `getVideosByAuthor`. `markNotificationsRead` additionally throws `FunnelcakeApiException(statusCode: 200, …)` on `200` with `success: false`. Add `isAvailable` guard parity. Update doc comments to canonical "Throws: …" blocks. |
| `mobile/packages/funnelcake_api_client/test/src/funnelcake_api_client_notification_test.dart` | Reshape obsolete silent-fail tests to throws-assertions; add new tests for `FunnelcakeNotConfiguredException`, `FunnelcakeTimeoutException`, and the `200 / success:false` soft-failure throw (with and without an `error` string). |
| `mobile/packages/notification_repository/lib/src/notification_repository.dart` | Replace `return NotificationPage.empty;` with `rethrow;` after the existing `developer.log`. Update dartdoc to document the rethrow contract. |
| `mobile/packages/notification_repository/test/src/notification_repository_test.dart` | Reshape `returns empty page on API error` → `rethrows on API error after logging` with assertion that `BehaviorSubject` preserves prior value across the throw. Add a `markAsRead` test pinning the soft-failure rollback contract end-to-end. |

No BLoC changes, no UI changes, no l10n changes — every consuming layer was already correct.

## Out of scope (deferred)

- **`_request<T>` helper extraction across all 24 methods**: #3586's scope.
- **Legacy provider/screen deletion**: #4208's scope.
- **`notification_repository` CI workflow**: this package was added in #4247 and has no dedicated workflow yet; flagged for a separate adjacent change.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] 🧹 Code refactor

## Test plan

- [x] `dart format` — 0 changed
- [x] `flutter analyze packages/funnelcake_api_client packages/notification_repository` — no issues
- [x] `flutter test packages/funnelcake_api_client/test/src/funnelcake_api_client_notification_test.dart` — 22/22 pass (includes 2 new soft-failure throw tests)
- [x] `flutter test packages/notification_repository/test/src/notification_repository_test.dart` — 66/66 pass (includes new soft-failure rollback test)
- [x] `flutter test test/notifications test/blocs/notifications` — 116/116 pass
- [ ] Manual on iOS: Repros A, B, C with airplane mode toggling; Repro D against a server returning `200 / success:false`
- [ ] Manual on Android: same four reproductions
- [ ] Manual account-switch: sign out / sign in as different user with no notifications → confirm empty state still renders as "No notifications yet" (because the API returns 200 with an empty list and `success: true`, not a soft-failure)

title: Inconsistent error handling in notification methods
body:
**Problem**

`getNotifications` and `markNotificationsRead` silently suppress all errors and return empty/failure responses, while every other method throws typed exceptions.

**Evidence**

`mobile/packages/funnelcake_api_client/lib/src/funnelcake_api_client.dart` lines 1857–1873: `on Object { return const NotificationResponse(...); }`. Callers of notification methods cannot distinguish between "no notifications" and "network failure."

**Done well**

Every other method in the same file (e.g., `getVideosByAuthor`, lines 170–208) correctly throws typed `FunnelcakeApiException`, allowing callers to distinguish errors from empty results.

**Related**

See "Massive boilerplate duplication in FunnelcakeApiClient" in [issues-code-quality.md](docs/code-review/issues-code-quality.md). The notification methods deviate from the shared pattern. Extracting a shared `_request<T>` helper would enforce consistent error handling across all methods, including these.

**Impact**

Medium. The caller has no way to show error UI or retry because the error is silently hidden.

**Effort**

Low. Make these methods throw like the rest, or document the intentional deviation with a clear reason.

**Source**: [Code Review — Error Handling](docs/code-review/issues-error-handling.md)

title: techdebt(notifications): consolidate dedupe substrates (retire _knownSourceEventIds + acceptRealtime id-equality fallback)
body:
## Summary

PR #4281 (closing #4264) adds a third dedupe gate (`NotificationItem.sourceEventIds` overlap inside `_emitSnapshotForPage`) on top of the two gates already in `NotificationRepository`. Reviewer flagged this as untracked dedupe-substrate debt — file a concrete follow-up so the consolidation isn't left as "if reviewers ask."

## Parent

- `#4200` (epic: stabilize in-app notifications, unread state, and push delivery)

## Related

- `#4204` / `#4247` (introduced `_knownSourceEventIds` for the REST → WS direction)
- `#4264` / `#4281` (introduced `sourceEventIds` on rendered items for the WS → REST direction)

## Problem

After PR #4281 lands, `NotificationRepository` carries three dedupe substrates that all encode the same Nostr-event-id identity:

1. **`_knownSourceEventIds: Set<String>`** — process-lifetime set at `notification_repository.dart:75`, written in `_enrichAndGroup` at `:524`, read by `acceptRealtime` at `:260`.
2. **`acceptRealtime` id-equality path** — `if (current.items.any((n) => n.id == newItem.id)) return;` at `:267`. Catches WS → WS but is redundant with substrate (1) for the REST → WS direction.
3. **`NotificationItem.sourceEventIds`** — new typed field on the rendered item, read by `_mergeAppendedPage` at `:408`, the source of truth for the cross-path identity going forward.

(3) is the principled source of truth: it's typed, asserted on the rendered item, exposed in `Equatable.props`, and covered by both model and repository tests. (1) is process-state with no visibility into refresh semantics — items that were in a previous snapshot but evicted by `refresh()` still block WS arrivals indefinitely. (2) is a legacy by-id check that does not see the cross-path identity.

This is dual-path tech debt: any future change to how the repository represents notification identity has to be made in three places to stay correct.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_knownSourceEventIds` field and its writes/reads are removed.
- [ ] `acceptRealtime`'s cross-path check at `:260` reads from the current snapshot's `sourceEventIds` set instead of the process-lifetime set.
- [ ] `acceptRealtime`'s id-equality fallback at `:267` either: (a) is replaced by a `sourceEventIds`-overlap check on the snapshot, or (b) is documented in code as the deliberate WS → WS gate with no cross-path responsibility.
- [ ] **PR #4247's load-bearing test** at `notification_repository_test.dart:1611` (`acceptRealtime dedupes a WS arrival whose id matches a REST item's sourceEventId`) still passes verbatim. This test is the regression guard — see `.claude/skills/tests-guard-intentional-workarounds`.
- [ ] All four `WS-first dedupe in page-merge (#4264)` tests still pass.
- [ ] A new test covers the semantic boundary the consolidation crosses: `refresh()` evicts an item from the snapshot → a subsequent WS arrival for that same Nostr event is **accepted** (because the server's authoritative first page no longer carries it, so it's genuinely new info now). This is the deliberate behavior change; pin it with a test so future readers see it isn't an accidental regression of substrate (1).

## Out of Scope

- Changing `NotificationItem.id` (still the `mark-as-read` server contract — tracked under `#4208`).
- Touching the `_mergeIntoExistingVideoGroup` / `_mergeAppendedVideoGroup` merge semantics — locked in PR #4281.

## Estimated Complexity

Low to medium. Bounded blast radius: ~4 code sites + 1 new test. Risk concentrates in the `refresh()`-then-WS edge case above.

title: techdebt(uploads): client-side byte/dimension guard for image uploads
body:
## Summary

Profile avatar and banner pickers currently rely on `image_picker`'s
`maxWidth`/`maxHeight`/`imageQuality` arguments to constrain image
size, plus the server-side 413 → `fileTooLarge` mapping as the
fallback. There is **no explicit client-side byte cap before
dispatching the upload event**, so very large gallery picks still
go through the full local processing pipeline (`BlossomUploadService`
metadata strip + read-into-memory for hashing + upload attempt)
before the server-side limit rejects them.

PR #4232 brought the banner picker up to the "at minimum" bar
suggested in review (bound both axes via `maxWidth: 1500,
maxHeight: 500`, extracted to named constants in
`mobile/lib/screens/profile_setup_screen.dart`). This issue tracks
the broader follow-up: an explicit client-side guard that short-
circuits before any processing/upload work happens.

## Scope

Audit and add a client-side byte/dimension guard for image uploads
across these picker sites:

- `mobile/lib/screens/profile_setup_screen.dart` — avatar picker (`_pickXFile`, ~`maxWidth: 1024, maxHeight: 1024`)
- `mobile/lib/screens/profile_setup_screen.dart` — banner picker (`_BannerActionRow._pickBannerImage`, `maxWidth: 1500, maxHeight: 500`)
- Any other in-app `image_picker` call sites that hand bytes/files to `BlossomUploadService` (e.g. video thumbnail flows, bug-report image attach added in #3094 / #3301) — confirm during audit.

Approach options to consider (decide during implementation):

1. A shared `ImageUploadValidator` (repository layer) that takes
   `Uint8List` / `File` + a `kind` (avatar/banner/thumbnail) and
   either passes or returns a typed failure (`tooLarge`,
   `unsupportedFormat`, etc.).
2. A per-kind `maxBytes` constant consumed by both the picker's
   post-pick check and the bloc/event handler.

Either way, the failure path should map to the existing
`PendingPictureError` / `BannerUploadError` enums so UI snackbar
copy is unchanged.

## Notes

- Keep this layer **above** `BlossomUploadService` so it short-
  circuits before metadata strip / hashing / network.
- The server-side 413 mapping stays as the fallback — this guard
  is a UX improvement, not a security boundary.
- Belongs in a shared validator / repository helper, not in the
  screen widget — the screen owns UI, not upload policy
  (`.claude/rules/architecture.md`).
- While auditing, the avatar picker still uses magic numbers
  (`1024`, `1024`, `85`); banner picker now uses named constants.
  Worth extracting matching `_maxAvatarImage*` constants in the
  same change for symmetry (`.claude/rules/code_style.md` →
  "No Hardcoded Values").

## Context

Raised during review of PR #4232:
- https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4232#issuecomment-4425808072

PR #4232 implemented the "at minimum" half of the original
suggestion (bound both axes). This issue covers the stronger
half (client-side byte cap) deferred from that PR to keep its
scope focused on banner-upload UI.

title: refactor(notifications): retire legacy list-item + dead screen (#3567)
body:
Closes #3567.

## Summary

Delete the legacy `NotificationListItem` widget at `lib/widgets/` and
its sole remaining call site, the dead `NotificationsScreen` at
`lib/screens/`. The BLoC dispatcher at
`lib/notifications/widgets/notification_list_item.dart` becomes the
single source of truth for notification row rendering.

## Why now — and why not folded into #4208

The prior `2026-05-11-issue4204-unify-unread-state` brainstorm
recommended deferring all legacy-file deletion to #4208 ("Last
execution item under notifications"), citing potential merge
conflicts with the still-open sibling issues #4205 (routing),
#4206 (row styling), and #4207 (push):

> If `#4205` (routing) / `#4206` (row styling) / `#4207` (push) land
> in parallel, the deletion creates merge conflicts. Sequencing
> #4208 last is exactly the mitigation.

That reasoning targeted a **bundled** deletion (the brainstorm's
Approach C) that would have touched both the legacy files and the
shared `relay_notifications_provider` / `notification_model_converter`
surface. This PR is **narrow** — legacy widget + dead screen + their
tests + mechanical router-test import swaps. None of the deleted or
edited files intersect #4205 / #4206 / #4207's BLoC-path work, so
the conflict premise does not apply.

Doing this now satisfies #3567's AC #2 (no call site references the
legacy widget) and reduces #4208's eventual diff by ~700 LOC + 4
tests, improving its reviewability when it lands.

## Description

Implements **#1602** — local **follow/save hashtags** for quick navigation: persist hashtag lists on device, **merge hashtag sources into the Following home feed** (with dedup and ordering aligned to existing repository behavior), and ship the **UI surfaces** from the design alignment docs (Explore/Popular tags context, search tags + filter, hashtag screen **More** menu, **Profile → Saved** with **Videos | Tags**).

### Behavior (high level)

- **Persistence (MVP):** There is **no backend** for hashtag subscriptions yet. Follow/save state is **stored only on the device** (local persistence in the app), so it does not sync across installs or devices until a server-backed model exists.
- **`followed_hashtags_repository`** (new package): normalized labels, profile-saved vs optional **Following-feed** hashtag sets, streams for reactive updates, cleanup hooks.
- **`videos_repository` / `VideoFeedBloc`**: Following feed coordinates people + curated lists with **hashtag-backed fetches**; handles empty-state edge cases when only hashtags are followed.
- **Hashtag screen**: **More** sheet — save/remove in profile, optional add/remove in Following feed (feature-flagged where applicable); snackbars and copy per product notes.
- **Discovery & search**: tags in **Explore** / **Popular** adjacency, **search** tag sections and **Tags** filter mode (query-narrowed), shared chip affordances where applicable.
- **Profile (own)**: fourth tab uses **`ProfileOwnSavedTab`** — filters **Videos** (bookmarked via `ProfileSavedGrid`) and **Tags** (`ProfileFollowedHashtagsGrid`); second tab icon remains **likes** (heart), not bookmarks.

### Verification (suggested)

From `mobile/`: `flutter analyze`; `flutter test` for touched areas — at minimum `test/blocs/video_feed/video_feed_bloc_test.dart`, `packages/followed_hashtags_repository/test/`, `test/widgets/profile/profile_followed_hashtags_grid_test.dart`, `test/widgets/hashtag_feed_more_menu_verification_test.dart`, and any updated search/explore tests.
